9. $\mathrm{C}_2\mathrm{H}_4 + 3\mathrm{O}_2 \rightarrow 2\mathrm{CO}_2 + 2\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}$
1 volume of $\mathrm{C}_2\mathrm{H}_4$ requires 3 volumes of $\mathrm{O}_2$ and
gives 2 volumes of $\mathrm{CO}_2$.
$\Rightarrow$ 300 volume of $\mathrm{C}_2\mathrm{H}_4$ requires 900 volume of
$\mathrm{O}_2$ and gives 400 volume of $\mathrm{CO}_2$.
Hence, the correct option is (d).

$= 22.4 \text{ l at STP}$
Hence, the correct option is (b).

**13.** $\mathrm{CaCO}_3 \rightarrow \mathrm{CaO} + \mathrm{CO}_2$
100 g of $\mathrm{CaCO}_3$ gives $22.4\lambda$ of $\mathrm{CO}_2$ at STP.
$x$ g of $\mathrm{CaCO}_3$ gives $33.6\lambda$ of $\mathrm{CO}_2$ at STP.
$\Rightarrow x = \frac{100 \times 33.6}{22.4} = 150$ g of 100% $\mathrm{CaCO}_3$
$\therefore \% \text{ purity} = \frac{150}{175} \times 100 = 85.7\%.$
Hence, the correct option is (b).

14. 96 g of X $\rightarrow$ $9 \times 10^{23}$ molecules
$a$ g of X $\rightarrow$ $6 \times 10^{23}$ molecules
$\therefore a = \frac{96 \times 6 \times 10^{23}}{9 \times 10^{23}}$
$a = 64$ g
$\therefore$ GMM of X = 64 g
0.32 g of Y $\rightarrow$ $1.2 \times 10^{22}$ molecules
$b$ g of Y $\rightarrow$ $6 \times 10^{23}$ molecules
$\Rightarrow b = \frac{0.32 \times 6 \times 10^{23}}{1.2 \times 10^{22}}$
$b = 16$ g
$\therefore$ GMM of Y = 16 g
According to Graham’s law $\frac{\mathrm{rX}}{\mathrm{rY}} = \sqrt{\frac{\mathrm{GMM}_Y}{\mathrm{GMM}_X}}$
$\Rightarrow \frac{\mathrm{rX}}{\mathrm{rY}} = \sqrt{\frac{16}{64}} = \frac{1}{2} \Rightarrow \mathrm{rY} = 2\mathrm{rX}$
Hence, the correct option is (b).
